title: logged model tag upsert: dedupe tag keys before _bulk_upsert so the last value wins on Postgres
answers: Setting tags on a logged model fails on Postgres when the same tag key is passed twice in one call
Where are logged model tags overwritten, and how are duplicate tag keys resolved?
Adding a bulk upsert for another table with a composite primary key: what must happen to repeated keys?
body:
Path: mlflow/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store.py:SqlAlchemyStore.set_logged_model_tags handles writing or overwriting tags on a logged model (the set-tags path taking a list of LoggedModelTag). It checks the model exists via _get_logged_model_record, then writes all of that model_id's tags in one session through _bulk_upsert into SqlLoggedModelTag.
Rule: Collapse the input to a dict keyed by tag.key before building the rows passed to _bulk_upsert, so the last occurrence of a key wins. A single INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (model_id, tag_key) DO UPDATE cannot touch the same row twice, so duplicates must be removed in Python first.
Symptom: On PostgreSQL, setting logged model tags where the same key appeared twice in one call failed with CardinalityViolation ("ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE command cannot affect row a second time"). The earlier session.merge loop silently kept the last value, and SQLite and MySQL still do.
Constraints: Applies to any caller of _bulk_upsert whose input can repeat a composite key. The dedupe preserves last-value-wins behavior. Does not cover delete_logged_model_tag.
applies: Logged model tag writes in the SQLAlchemy tracking store, and any new _bulk_upsert caller whose input may repeat a key.

search: Logged model tag writes in the SQLAlchemy tracking store: duplicate tag keys are collapsed into a dict before the bulk upsert so the last value wins, avoiding a Postgres ON CONFLICT error when a key repeats in one call. Applies to any bulk upsert whose input may repeat a composite key. Does not cover tag deletion.
